**Kevin George Knipfing** (born April 26, 1965) known professionally as **Kevin James**, is an American actor, comedian, writer and producer. James began his career as a stand-up comedian on Long Island in the late 1980s before rising to prominence for playing Doug Heffernan on the CBS sitcom _The King of Queens_ (1998–2007), for which he received a nomination for Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series in 2006.

In 2004, James made his first film appearance in _50 First Dates_, and the following year co-starred in _Hitch_. He went on to star in _I Now Pronounce You Chuck & Larry_ (2007), _Paul Blart: Mall Cop_ (2009), _Grown Ups_ (2010), _Zookeeper_ (2011), _Here Comes the Boom_ (2012), and _Pixels_ (2015). He also voiced characters in the animated films _Monster House_, _Barnyard_ (both 2006), and _Hotel Transylvania_ (2012). He also was nominated for a [People's Choice Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Choice_Award "People's Choice Award") in 2017 for his role on the CBS sitcom _Kevin Can Wait_ (2016–2018). James also appeared in several dramatic roles, including _The Dilemma_ (2011), _Little Boy_ (2015), and _Becky_ (2020). In 2026, he starred in the romantic comedy _Solo Mio_.

Kevin George Knipfing was born in Mineola, New York, on April 26, 1965,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-filmref-1) to office worker Janet Klein and insurance agency owner Joseph Valentine Knipfing Jr. His father is of German ancestry, and his mother is Jewish.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-filmref-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-3) He grew up in Stony Brook, New York, with a sister named Leslie and an older brother named Gary, who also became a comedian and actor, adopting the stage name Gary Valentine.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-NYTimesusan-5) They were raised Catholic.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-6)
James graduated from Ward Melville High School in 1983,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-NYTimesusan-5) where he reached the top position on the wrestling team, one spot above his friend and future professional wrestler Mick Foley. Both wrestled in the Heavyweight weight class. When James suffered a season-ending back injury, Foley took over the first string position.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-hwoodreporter-7) Both men went on to study at the State University of New York at Cortland, where James played halfback on the varsity football team until another back injury permanently ended his sporting ambitions.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-NYTimesusan-5)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-msndotcom-8)

James began doing stand-up comedy in 1989, making his debut at Richie Minervini's East Side Comedy Club on Long Island.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-NYTimesusan-5) He also started performing comedy with a troupe at the club, during which time he adopted "James" as his stage surname in honor of his favorite school teacher.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-9) He gained popularity through numerous appearances on various talk shows, including _The Tonight Show with Jay Leno_, _Late Show with David Letterman_, _[Late Night with Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late\_Night\_with\_Conan\_O'Brien "Late Night with Conan O'Brien")_, _Dennis Miller Live_, _The Late Late Show_, _[The Rosie O'Donnell Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Rosie\_O'Donnell\_Show "The Rosie O'Donnell Show")_, _The Ellen DeGeneres Show_, and _Live with Regis and Kathie Lee_. James was listed at No. 76 on Comedy Central's list of the 100 Greatest Stand-Up Comedians. James has also done his stand-up routine on _Just for Laughs_, an annual comedy festival in Montreal, Quebec. Later he was on commercials for [Mazzio's Italian Eatery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazzio's "Mazzio's"). In 2001, James did his own stand-up special called _Kevin James: Sweat the Small Stuff_. He has also appeared as a musical guest on _Just for Laughs_. In 2018, James released another stand-up special on Netflix called _Kevin James: Never Don't Give Up_. In 2024, James released his third special on Amazon Prime Video called _Kevin James: Irregardless_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-10)

James' first television job was in 1991 on _The New Candid Camera_, where he used his comedy timing and improvisation skills playing the actor that pulled practical jokes on unsuspecting people. He appeared in _A&E's An Evening at the Improv_ in 1994.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-11) James appeared on television as the announcer for the MTV sports game show _SandBlast_ from 1994 to 1996._[citation needed_]
James later moved to Los Angeles and befriended Ray Romano, and he guest-starred on a few episodes of Romano's hit CBS sitcom, _Everybody Loves Raymond_. These appearances led to the development of his own sitcom, _The King of Queens_, which ran on CBS from September 21, 1998, to May 14, 2007, James played working class parcel delivery man Doug Heffernan who works for a company known as IPS. He is married to Carrie (Leah Remini), a sharp-tongued, ambitious secretary at a Manhattan law firm who is far less content with working-class life in Queens. Her obsessive, vindictive father, Arthur (Jerry Stiller), who is prone toward bizarre conduct, lives with them. For his work on the eighth season, James was nominated for a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series in 2006.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-12)

In 2007, he was the grand marshal for the Pepsi 400 promoting _I Now Pronounce You Chuck & Larry_ and saying "I just got three things to say: God bless our troops, God bless America and gentlemen, start your engines".[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-26) He did it again in June 2010 with friend and fellow actor Adam Sandler to promote _Grown Ups_, in 2012 at the fall Talladega race to promote _Here Comes the Boom_,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-27) and in July 2013 at the Coke-Zero 400 with co-stars Sandler and [Shaquille O'Neal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaquille_O'Neal "Shaquille O'Neal") to promote _Grown Ups 2_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-28) Both the 2007 Pepsi 400 command and June 2010 command at Michigan with Sandler have since been voted as two of the best and most memorable NASCAR commands in history by fans.
A web series titled _Dusty Peacock_ produced by James and starring his brother Gary Valentine began streaming on Crackle in July 2009.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-29)
In February 2020, James revived his YouTube channel which he had launched back on November 27, 2017[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-30) featuring short films "based on thin premises, like James eagerly waiting for a green light, misreading a hand wave, or spending birthdays by himself, but many carry a sense of melancholy and restraint."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-31) By June 2020, he had over 535,000 subscribers and 28 million total views.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-32)
James's wife Steffiana de la Cruz in 2011

James met Filipina-American model and actress Steffiana de la Cruz as part of a blind date, and they were married on June 19, 2004.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-33) They have four children together and reside in California.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-34)
Raised in a Catholic home, James stated in 2012 that he remains a devout Catholic.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-background-35) In 2019, he hosted a Catholic retreat featuring priest Chad Ripperger and theologian Scott Hahn.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-36) In a 2024 interview on _The Joe Rogan Experience_, he revealed that he fasted for 41.5 consecutive days, only subsisting on water containing salt all throughout. He did this out of religious devotion when one of his daughters was diagnosed with a neurobehavioral disorder.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-39)
James is a fan of the New York Mets baseball team and threw out the first pitch at a game in August 2024.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-40)

**Kevin George Knipfing** (born April 26, 1965) known professionally as **Kevin James**, is an American actor, comedian, writer and producer. James began his career as a stand-up comedian on Long Island in the late 1980s before rising to prominence for playing Doug Heffernan on the CBS sitcom _The King of Queens_ (1998–2007), for which he received a nomination for Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series in 2006.

texts.2:
Kevin George Knipfing was born in Mineola, New York, on April 26, 1965,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-filmref-1) to office worker Janet Klein and insurance agency owner Joseph Valentine Knipfing Jr. His father is of German ancestry, and his mother is Jewish.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-filmref-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-3) He grew up in Stony Brook, New York, with a sister named Leslie and an older brother named Gary, who also became a comedian and actor, adopting the stage name Gary Valentine.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-NYTimesusan-5) They were raised Catholic.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-6)
James graduated from Ward Melville High School in 1983,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-NYTimesusan-5) where he reached the top position on the wrestling team, one spot above his friend and future professional wrestler Mick Foley. Both wrestled in the Heavyweight weight class. When James suffered a season-ending back injury, Foley took over the first string position.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-hwoodreporter-7) Both men went on to study at the State University of New York at Cortland, where James played halfback on the varsity football team until another back injury permanently ended his sporting ambitions.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-NYTimesusan-5)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-msndotcom-8)
texts.3: James began doing stand-up comedy in 1989, making his debut at Richie Minervini's East Side Comedy Club on Long Island.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-NYTimesusan-5) He also started performing comedy with a troupe at the club, during which time he adopted "James" as his stage surname in honor of his favorite school teacher.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-9) He gained popularity through numerous appearances on various talk shows, including _The Tonight Show with Jay Leno_, _Late Show with David Letterman_, _[Late Night with Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late\_Night\_with\_Conan\_O'Brien "Late Night with Conan O'Brien")_, _Dennis Miller Live_, _The Late Late Show_, _[The Rosie O'Donnell Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Rosie\_O'Donnell\_Show "The Rosie O'Donnell Show")_, _The Ellen DeGeneres Show_, and _Live with Regis and Kathie Lee_. James was listed at No. 76 on Comedy Central's list of the 100 Greatest Stand-Up Comedians. James has also done his stand-up routine on _Just for Laughs_, an annual comedy festival in Montreal, Quebec. Later he was on commercials for [Mazzio's Italian Eatery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazzio's "Mazzio's"). In 2001, James did his own stand-up special called _Kevin James: Sweat the Small Stuff_. He has also appeared as a musical guest on _Just for Laughs_. In 2018, James released another stand-up special on Netflix called _Kevin James: Never Don't Give Up_. In 2024, James released his third special on Amazon Prime Video called _Kevin James: Irregardless_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-10)
texts.4:
James' first television job was in 1991 on _The New Candid Camera_, where he used his comedy timing and improvisation skills playing the actor that pulled practical jokes on unsuspecting people. He appeared in _A&E's An Evening at the Improv_ in 1994.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-11) James appeared on television as the announcer for the MTV sports game show _SandBlast_ from 1994 to 1996._[citation needed_]
James later moved to Los Angeles and befriended Ray Romano, and he guest-starred on a few episodes of Romano's hit CBS sitcom, _Everybody Loves Raymond_. These appearances led to the development of his own sitcom, _The King of Queens_, which ran on CBS from September 21, 1998, to May 14, 2007, James played working class parcel delivery man Doug Heffernan who works for a company known as IPS. He is married to Carrie (Leah Remini), a sharp-tongued, ambitious secretary at a Manhattan law firm who is far less content with working-class life in Queens. Her obsessive, vindictive father, Arthur (Jerry Stiller), who is prone toward bizarre conduct, lives with them. For his work on the eighth season, James was nominated for a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series in 2006.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-12)

In 2007, he was the grand marshal for the Pepsi 400 promoting _I Now Pronounce You Chuck & Larry_ and saying "I just got three things to say: God bless our troops, God bless America and gentlemen, start your engines".[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-26) He did it again in June 2010 with friend and fellow actor Adam Sandler to promote _Grown Ups_, in 2012 at the fall Talladega race to promote _Here Comes the Boom_,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-27) and in July 2013 at the Coke-Zero 400 with co-stars Sandler and [Shaquille O'Neal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaquille_O'Neal "Shaquille O'Neal") to promote _Grown Ups 2_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-28) Both the 2007 Pepsi 400 command and June 2010 command at Michigan with Sandler have since been voted as two of the best and most memorable NASCAR commands in history by fans.
A web series titled _Dusty Peacock_ produced by James and starring his brother Gary Valentine began streaming on Crackle in July 2009.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-29)
In February 2020, James revived his YouTube channel which he had launched back on November 27, 2017[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-30) featuring short films "based on thin premises, like James eagerly waiting for a green light, misreading a hand wave, or spending birthdays by himself, but many carry a sense of melancholy and restraint."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-31) By June 2020, he had over 535,000 subscribers and 28 million total views.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-32)

James met Filipina-American model and actress Steffiana de la Cruz as part of a blind date, and they were married on June 19, 2004.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-33) They have four children together and reside in California.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-34)
Raised in a Catholic home, James stated in 2012 that he remains a devout Catholic.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-background-35) In 2019, he hosted a Catholic retreat featuring priest Chad Ripperger and theologian Scott Hahn.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-36) In a 2024 interview on _The Joe Rogan Experience_, he revealed that he fasted for 41.5 consecutive days, only subsisting on water containing salt all throughout. He did this out of religious devotion when one of his daughters was diagnosed with a neurobehavioral disorder.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-39)

Kevin George Knipfing was born in Mineola, New York, on April 26, 1965,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-filmref-1) to office worker Janet Klein and insurance agency owner Joseph Valentine Knipfing Jr. His father is of German ancestry, and his mother is Jewish.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-filmref-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-3) He grew up in Stony Brook, New York, with a sister named Leslie and an older brother named Gary, who also became a comedian and actor, adopting the stage name Gary Valentine.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-NYTimesusan-5) They were raised Catholic.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-6)
James graduated from Ward Melville High School in 1983,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-NYTimesusan-5) where he reached the top position on the wrestling team, one spot above his friend and future professional wrestler Mick Foley. Both wrestled in the Heavyweight weight class. When James suffered a season-ending back injury, Foley took over the first string position.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-hwoodreporter-7) Both men went on to study at the State University of New York at Cortland, where James played halfback on the varsity football team until another back injury permanently ended his sporting ambitions.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-NYTimesusan-5)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-msndotcom-8)

James began doing stand-up comedy in 1989, making his debut at Richie Minervini's East Side Comedy Club on Long Island.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-NYTimesusan-5) He also started performing comedy with a troupe at the club, during which time he adopted "James" as his stage surname in honor of his favorite school teacher.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-9) He gained popularity through numerous appearances on various talk shows, including _The Tonight Show with Jay Leno_, _Late Show with David Letterman_, _[Late Night with Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late\_Night\_with\_Conan\_O'Brien "Late Night with Conan O'Brien")_, _Dennis Miller Live_, _The Late Late Show_, _[The Rosie O'Donnell Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Rosie\_O'Donnell\_Show "The Rosie O'Donnell Show")_, _The Ellen DeGeneres Show_, and _Live with Regis and Kathie Lee_. James was listed at No. 76 on Comedy Central's list of the 100 Greatest Stand-Up Comedians. James has also done his stand-up routine on _Just for Laughs_, an annual comedy festival in Montreal, Quebec. Later he was on commercials for [Mazzio's Italian Eatery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazzio's "Mazzio's"). In 2001, James did his own stand-up special called _Kevin James: Sweat the Small Stuff_. He has also appeared as a musical guest on _Just for Laughs_. In 2018, James released another stand-up special on Netflix called _Kevin James: Never Don't Give Up_. In 2024, James released his third special on Amazon Prime Video called _Kevin James: Irregardless_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-10)

James' first television job was in 1991 on _The New Candid Camera_, where he used his comedy timing and improvisation skills playing the actor that pulled practical jokes on unsuspecting people. He appeared in _A&E's An Evening at the Improv_ in 1994.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-11) James appeared on television as the announcer for the MTV sports game show _SandBlast_ from 1994 to 1996._[citation needed_]
James later moved to Los Angeles and befriended Ray Romano, and he guest-starred on a few episodes of Romano's hit CBS sitcom, _Everybody Loves Raymond_. These appearances led to the development of his own sitcom, _The King of Queens_, which ran on CBS from September 21, 1998, to May 14, 2007, James played working class parcel delivery man Doug Heffernan who works for a company known as IPS. He is married to Carrie (Leah Remini), a sharp-tongued, ambitious secretary at a Manhattan law firm who is far less content with working-class life in Queens. Her obsessive, vindictive father, Arthur (Jerry Stiller), who is prone toward bizarre conduct, lives with them. For his work on the eighth season, James was nominated for a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series in 2006.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-12)

In 2007, he was the grand marshal for the Pepsi 400 promoting _I Now Pronounce You Chuck & Larry_ and saying "I just got three things to say: God bless our troops, God bless America and gentlemen, start your engines".[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-26) He did it again in June 2010 with friend and fellow actor Adam Sandler to promote _Grown Ups_, in 2012 at the fall Talladega race to promote _Here Comes the Boom_,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-27) and in July 2013 at the Coke-Zero 400 with co-stars Sandler and [Shaquille O'Neal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaquille_O'Neal "Shaquille O'Neal") to promote _Grown Ups 2_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-28) Both the 2007 Pepsi 400 command and June 2010 command at Michigan with Sandler have since been voted as two of the best and most memorable NASCAR commands in history by fans.
A web series titled _Dusty Peacock_ produced by James and starring his brother Gary Valentine began streaming on Crackle in July 2009.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-29)
In February 2020, James revived his YouTube channel which he had launched back on November 27, 2017[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-30) featuring short films "based on thin premises, like James eagerly waiting for a green light, misreading a hand wave, or spending birthdays by himself, but many carry a sense of melancholy and restraint."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-31) By June 2020, he had over 535,000 subscribers and 28 million total views.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-32)
James's wife Steffiana de la Cruz in 2011

James met Filipina-American model and actress Steffiana de la Cruz as part of a blind date, and they were married on June 19, 2004.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-33) They have four children together and reside in California.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-34)
Raised in a Catholic home, James stated in 2012 that he remains a devout Catholic.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-background-35) In 2019, he hosted a Catholic retreat featuring priest Chad Ripperger and theologian Scott Hahn.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-36) In a 2024 interview on _The Joe Rogan Experience_, he revealed that he fasted for 41.5 consecutive days, only subsisting on water containing salt all throughout. He did this out of religious devotion when one of his daughters was diagnosed with a neurobehavioral disorder.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-39)
James is a fan of the New York Mets baseball team and threw out the first pitch at a game in August 2024.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_James#cite_note-40)
